idiom_name: sorted milestone array + hand-written lower bound over Date (or Temporal.PlainDate)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no ordered map with a floor lookup - Map iterates in insertion order and object keys compare by identity - so the milestone store is an array kept sorted by effective date, read with Array.prototype.findLast (ES2023) for short histories or a hand-written binary search for long ones, and the owner exposes valueAt(when) plus a default currentValue() form. Date is the historical Time Point but it is mutable, time-zone sensitive and conflates calendar date with instant; the TC39 Temporal proposal (Temporal.PlainDate for date-only values) is what the pattern should use once the runtime provides it, with Date reserved for persisted instants. What replaces the classic structure: nothing structural - the collection is a plain array plus a function - so the pattern has to be written as a small explicit module rather than emerging from the language.
pitfalls: new Date('2024-01-01') parses as UTC midnight while new Date(2024, 0, 1) is local midnight: a date-only history keyed by Date silently picks the previous or next version depending on the parsing form - store Temporal.PlainDate or 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings.

Date objects are mutable: setDate/setHours on a Date that a version holds rewrites that version (and every alias to it) in place, and Map keys compare by reference for objects, so two equal Dates are two different keys.
JSON round-trips turn Date into an ISO string without a type marker, so a persisted history reloaded from storage is keyed by strings that no longer compare with Dates.

Object property order is not date order and Array.prototype.sort compares strings by default: sort((a, b) => a.from - b.from) on dates works only by coercion, and a version inserted without re-sorting the array breaks the binary search silently.
